caption:
15% of your US dividends never make it into your TFSA, and you can't claim it back.

The Canada-US treaty keeps a list of retirement accounts. The RRSP is on it. The TFSA isn't.

So a US company pays $1,000. The border takes $150 on the way out. $850 lands in your tax-free box, and Canada can't refund the rest, because you owe nothing here to claim it against.

Same fund, same dividend. In an RRSP it arrives whole.

There's a catch, and it's the part that trips people up. The exemption covers US-listed holdings you hold directly. A Canadian-listed fund that owns US assets can still leak at the fund level, in either account.

So before your next buy, two things. What box it sits in, and what it actually holds.

General education, not tax advice. Confirm your own case with the CRA or a tax professional.

Save this one and check before your next buy.

fact.claim: US dividends held in a TFSA lose 15% at the border and it cannot be claimed back. The RRSP is exempt. Canadian-listed funds that hold US assets can still leak inside either.
